overview.title: Campus architecture in the mountains
overview.p1: Al Akhawayn University is one of Ifrane’s defining institutions — a modern campus set against the same cool climate and green planning that shape the town. Visitors usually see exteriors and public edges rather than a full interior tour.
overview.p2: Treat it as a short architectural and atmosphere stop: clean lines, mountain air and a contrast with medina cities. Respect campus rules and any access limits.
overview.p3: Fifteen to forty minutes is enough for most travellers. Combine with the stone lion and Source Vittel.

q1.question: Can I enter freely?
q1.answer: Public access varies — stay on allowed exterior areas and follow signage.

q2.question: Guided tours?
q2.answer: Not a standard tourist product; do not expect a museum-style circuit.

q3.question: How long?
q3.answer: Fifteen to forty minutes for an exterior look.

q4.question: Worth it?
q4.answer: Yes as part of understanding modern Ifrane — not as a standalone half-day.

q5.question: Photos?
q5.answer: Exterior photos are usually fine; avoid disrupting campus life.
